topic: Hilbert argues that the axiomatic method is indispensable in set theory, resolving the paradox of the set of all sets by denying that it is a consistent axiomatically definable set, and then considers how to order the voting when several motions are pending at the end of a debate, listing the 8 possible outcomes for 3 motions.

triage.modern_statement: This can't be pinned down as a precise question. The fragment asks only what happens 'if one excludes the distributive law'. It doesn't say which structure is meant: arithmetic or number systems, the segment arithmetic in Hilbert's geometry, the logical calculus (where dropping distributivity leads to non-distributive lattices or orthomodular 'quantum' logics), or Boolean set algebra. The page topics, set-theoretic paradoxes and the order of voting on motions, don't settle which one. A plausible generic reading would be 'what algebraic or logical theory remains, and what fails, when the distributive axiom is dropped from an axiom system (an independence or weakening question)?'. That reading is my conjecture, not something the note establishes.
